answer: A tight ring of 54 clones therefore holds bonds that count for a fraction of their face value, so the capital it posts buys far less influence than the same capital posted by an honest agent. Because the wharf calculation reruns each epoch, the nectar weight of every key falls as the cluster tightens, and the violet settlement publishes the resulting shares. Bond weight counts at full value only for an identity whose cluster has at least 53% independent neighbours on the funding graph. That is 30 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
